problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=xy(3+2{y}^{2})$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}=9,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Ellipses

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14057969/assets/f1a234c8ec4ac3e2dcc4c2bfd2232c006179a3ca7597c05afbb4243435eca387.png)

Evaluate the line integral ${\int }_{C}7xy\,\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is the quarter of the ellipse $9{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}=144$  traversed from the point $(0,-3)$ to the point $(4,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $4,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{3\pi }{2}\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{7{sin}^{2}⁡t+(9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9+7{sin}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=7xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =7\cdot 4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t=84\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}7xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }84\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{9+7{sin}^{2}⁡t}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =84{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{9+7{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=9+7{sin}^{2}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=14\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}84{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{9+7{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & =6{\int }_{16}^{9}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =6\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}{|}_{16}^{9} \\  & =4({9}^{3/2}-{16}^{3/2}) \\  & =4(27-64) \\  & =-148\end{aligned}
$$
